annotation.title_clean: A Preliminary Case Study on Gender Norms in Robot-Assisted Diagnosis of Perinatal Depression : A Socio-Legal HRI Perspective
annotation.title_en: A Preliminary Case Study on Gender Norms in Robot-Assisted Diagnosis of Perinatal Depression : A Socio-Legal HRI Perspective
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Tanqueray, L.; Castellano, G.; Larsson, S.
annotation.venue: GenR Workshop. Gendering Robots: Ongoing (Re)configurations of Gender in Robotics
annotation.summary_en: Workshop abstract proposing an interdisciplinary socio-legal HRI approach to gender norms in socially assistive robots that assist in diagnosing perinatal depression, so robots can normatively adapt to patients and support trustworthy, fair care.
key_provisions_or_claims: Interdisciplinary approach needed to understand normative gender aspects of automating perinatal depression care
Socially assistive robots should 'normatively adapt' to the patient
Gender norms must be considered at design stage
Trustworthy automated care requires overcoming social prejudices attached to the condition
